segments: The tenth dynasty.
Arab kings.
he loved greatly Banafsheh (Banafar).
And the wife of the Caliph became jealous of her, that is, of the handmaid,
and she enticed the son of the Caliph (her son):
and she made him lie with her, that is, with the handmaid.
And when the Caliph sought her as usual,
his wife said to him:
"She is no longer lawful for you,
because your son has slept with her."
Now when the Caliph heard what had happened,
he was perturbed and his mind was agitated, and he became enraged (against his son),
and commanded in fury that his son should be killed.
The nobles, however, did the opposite:
that is, they killed him,
and set up his son in his place.
[He reigned] nine years.
When those nobles had put al-Mustanjid to death by such a death as this,
they chose one of his sons,
one whose hope of the caliphate was cut off,
because of his mildness and modesty.
And they made him swear that he would not kill any of them,
and that he would restore to them everything that his father had taken from them.
And when he had sworn to them,
they brought his brother,
and by force and threats of death made him swear,
and likewise all the members of his family.
And they too swore to him,
and proclaimed him al-Mustadi'.
And in the year 1483,
1483 of the Greeks,
heavy snow fell throughout all the land,
so that even in India, where they had never seen snow at all,
fourteen cubits of snow fell, as it is reported.
And the rivers and springs froze,
and animals and birds perished from hunger and thirst.
And human beings were also shut up in their houses as if in graves,
and they could not even go from village to village;
and many tent-dwellers and travelers on the roads were suffocated in the snow.
Now in Sebastia, when the famine grew exceedingly severe
by reason of the blockage of the roads,
the nobles demanded of Isma'il, son of Danishmand, the ruler of Cappadocia, that he give grain to them and to their people,
so that they might be sustained until the summer and not die,
because many storehouses of wheat were gathered for him.
And when he was stingy and would not give,
they gathered against him and killed him and his wife,
who was the sister of Sultan Qilij Arslan,
and five hundred persons from his household, his servants, and his handmaids;
and they seized his treasuries.
And they sent to Damascus and brought Dhu'l-Nun his uncle,
who was there 24
